_interpretation: BLEU-1 lifts +16.7% over 50K baseline at only 2K steps; this is consistent with the alpha=12 early-curriculum pulling CE loss harder than the original 50K run sees in its early/mid bands.
Phi_final sits +1.12 above the 50K final phi (45.73 vs 44.61). Higher is better (further from threshold 5.0); the 2K run did NOT erode phi.
Phi baseline difference (-0.10) is within rounding of float-stable matmul order / cuDNN nondeterminism; chain-of-custody on qmirror seed itself is bit-exact verified.

_band_rationale: Lower bound 0.005: ablation_A_50k F1=0.00586 (32-prompt subset) is the empirical floor.
Upper bound 0.012: 2x ablation_A baseline; loosely informed by ablation_B_seed42 outlier (0.0120) which was the high end of the 4-seed P1.5 ensemble distribution.
Both bounds are 1-shot empirical, not statistical CIs. A strict equivalence test would require >=3 paired (qmirror vs seed=42) runs at matching step counts.

honest_caveats_c3: Step-count mismatch: 2K vs 50K is 25x. The +16.7% BLEU-1 delta is interpretable as 'qmirror seeding does not collapse training' but NOT as 'qmirror beats determinism'. A step-matched 2K control with seed=42 would be the proper apples-to-apples comparison.

Quantum provenance is via deterministic HMAC-DRBG expansion of a one-shot quantum measurement; the per-step uint32 draws are not live quantum samples. The cond.4 attestation only certifies the EXPANDED stream's statistical quality, not per-call quantum-ness.

Single-run, single-seed-source result. The 'no anomaly' verdict means 'this one run lands in the empirical band'; it does not statistically falsify a hypothesis like 'qmirror seeding shifts BLEU-1 distribution by sigma > 0.001'.
